editorial:
Imagine landing your dream job at the biggest tech company in the world. That is exactly what happens to Mae, a young woman who starts working at a place called The Circle. At first, it feels like a paradise with free food and cool gadgets. But as you watch her get promoted, you start to realize that the company wants every single second of her life to be public. The vibe is a bit creepy because it shows how easy it is to give up your privacy for likes and followers. You will feel the tension build as Mae becomes the face of the company and starts ignoring her own friends and family just to fit in.

While the pacing starts a bit slow, the acting is solid and makes you really worry for Mae. The best part is how it makes you think about your own phone and social media habits. It is not a high-action flick, but it keeps you interested with its scary ideas about the future. If you want the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick for anyone who likes stories about big corporations and secrets.
endingExplained: At the end, the company tries to force Mae to live her entire life on camera 24/7. They even want to use the tech to watch everyone in the world. Mae realizes this is wrong and uses the system to expose the company's secrets. She reveals their private data to the public during a big live stream. In the end, she breaks free from their control, showing that privacy is more important than fame.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about technology and privacy.
